title: Technical English — Course 3, Semester 1 — Pilot Variant 2

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. Where can students collect the worksheet?
tasks.audioText: The drawing office has updated the worksheet for dimension reading. Students should collect a copy from Room 8 before the lesson on Thursday. The instructor will explain the difference between overall dimensions and hole spacing. A short practice task will follow, and students may use the metric conversion table provided on the last page.

tasks.prompt: A technician checked a component drawing before preparing an inspection record. The overall length was shown as 120 millimetres, while the width was 45 millimetres. Two holes were positioned at equal distances from the centre line. The technician recorded the measurements in the same units as the drawing and noted that the drawing revision number had to be included in the report. Reading 1. What was the overall length?
Why did the technician record the revision number?
options: To identify the technician who measured the component
To identify the exact version of the drawing

tasks.prompt: The width of the plate ___ as 45 millimetres on the drawing.
Choose TWO details that should be checked when reading a technical drawing.
options: The colour of the paper clip
The name of an unrelated website

tasks.prompt: A number or code that identifies the current version of a drawing is a revision ___.
A dimension is difficult to read. What should you ask?
options: I will guess the value and continue.
Could you help me confirm this dimension on the latest drawing?
I will change the drawing myself.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of technical dimensions in a logical order.
options: Check the drawing title and revision
correctOrder: Check the drawing title and revision

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words explaining how to read and record dimensions from a technical drawing. Mention units, revision control and one possible source of error.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: the response explains how to read and record dimensions, including units (0–2); it addresses checking the drawing revision and identifies one plausible source of measurement/reading error (0–2); instructions are clear with understandable grammar (0–2); dimension/revision vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are accurate (0–2).
